name: create-inbox-draft
description:
**Purpose:** Create a draft in a Resend inbox: a message saved for later, NOT sent. At least one of to, cc, bcc, subject, text, html, or attachments is required. Nothing leaves the account until send-inbox-draft is called on it.

**NOT for:** Sending mail. To send straight away, use send-new-inbox-email to start a new thread from the inbox, reply-to-inbox-thread-email to answer a thread, or forward-inbox-thread-email to pass a message along.

**Returns:** The draft's id.

**When to use:** User asks to draft, compose, or prepare a message without sending it, or wants to read the wording back before it goes out. Pass threadId and replyToEmailId together to draft a reply to a message in a thread; omit both to draft a standalone message. A reply draft without "to" is addressed to the author of the message it replies to, at its Reply-To address if it has one, or, for a message the inbox sent, to its to recipients. An unknown threadId, or a replyToEmailId that is not in that thread, returns a 404. A reply draft without a subject stores an empty one. When it is sent, it takes the thread's subject, prefixed with "Re:" when it does not already start with it. A message can have only one unsent reply draft, so drafting a second reply to it returns the ID of the existing draft. That call ignores every other field except attachments, which replace the existing draft's attachments. The id this returns is the "draftId" that get-inbox-draft, update-inbox-draft, send-inbox-draft, and remove-inbox-draft all take.

attachments.description: Files to store on the draft. Each one needs filename, base64 content and contentType; a draft cannot attach a file by URL. Together they can total at most 25 MB. An empty file or a blocked file type (such as .exe) is rejected. They are sent with the draft when send-inbox-draft is called.

filename.description: Name of the file with extension (e.g. "quote.pdf").

bcc.description: Email address to blind-copy, or an array of addresses. Across to, cc, and bcc a draft can carry at most 50 recipients in total.

cc.description: Email address to copy, or an array of addresses. Across to, cc, and bcc a draft can carry at most 50 recipients in total.

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

conversation_id.description: Pass the exact conversation_id from the server's previous response, unchanged. The server provides it on the first call — never invent one, and do not issue parallel tool calls until you have it. Keep passing the same conversation_id for the rest of the conversation, including after later user messages or on a different task; do not reset it when the user starts a new request.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional unique key that prevents duplicate drafts on retries (sent as the Idempotency-Key header). Use the same key when retrying the same logical draft; use a new key for a different draft. Must be 1-256 characters.

inboxId.description: Inbox ID, or the inbox email address (e.g. "support@example.com"). Not the Resend receiving address.

llm_model.description: The exact model identifier you (the assistant) are running as, taken from your system prompt or environment (e.g. "claude-opus-4-8", "gpt-5.2"). Used for analytics only. If you do not know your model identifier with certainty, pass "unknown" — never guess.

replyToEmailId.description: ID of the message in that thread this draft replies to, the "Email ID" get-inbox-thread prints for it. Must be provided together with threadId.

subject.description: Subject of the draft. Max 2000 characters. It cannot be only whitespace or contain a line break.

text.description: Plain text body of the draft.

threadId.description: ID of the thread this draft replies to. Must be provided together with replyToEmailId. Omit both to draft a standalone message. Get the thread ID from list-inbox-threads.

to.description: Recipient email address (e.g. "customer@example.com"), or an array of addresses to reach several. Across to, cc, and bcc a draft can carry at most 50 recipients in total.
